MPPSC-2021-068.basis: Clarified to a single false statement: Sipahi Bahadur Sarkar was set up at Sehore (14 Jan 1858), not Indore. The other three statements are true.

MPPSC-2022-003.basis: The stored key D (Dartmouth) is a place, not a person. John McCarthy coined the term, ran the Dartmouth workshop and created LISP, and is the father of AI.

MPPSC-2022-018.basis: The Lifetime Dronacharya for hockey 2020 went to Romesh Pathania; Jude Felix got the regular (not lifetime) award.

MPPSC-2022-053.basis: Both NHRC statements are true and neither explains the other, so the inclusive option D is the answer.

MPPSC-2022-083.basis: MP is the fifth largest iron ore producer (~2%), not third, so statement A is the false one. Statement D is true: Chhattisgarh took most of the reserves on separation.

MPPSC-2022-090.basis: The Narmada has cut the deep gorge between the Akhrani and Mathwar hills, not the Chambal.

MPPSC-2023-001.basis: The order is soil preparation, sowing, irrigation, harvesting; irrigation cannot precede sowing.

MPPSC-2023-009.basis: Osteoclasts are the bone-resorbing cells involved in fracture remodelling; bone formation is osteoblast work.

MPPSC-2023-046.basis: Flipkart, Alibaba and Amazon sell business-to-consumer, so B2C.

MPPSC-2023-052.basis: The Gaza Strip lies on the Mediterranean coast.

MPPSC-2023-057.basis: The Vaitarna rises on the Trimbak-Anjaneri hills near Trimbakeshwar in Nashik district.

MPPSC-2023-059.basis: The first successful tapping of underground heat for district heating was at Boise, Idaho, in 1892.

MPPSC-2024-018.basis: The Atal Bihari Vajpayee Institute of Good Governance and Policy Analysis is in Bhopal.

MPPSC-2024-029.basis: The MP tribal self-employment scheme is the Bhagwan Birsa Munda Self-Employment Scheme; Tantya Mama is a separate welfare scheme.

MPPSC-2024-072.basis: Jharkhand (~26%) and Odisha (~25%) together exceed half of India's coal reserves.

MPPSC-2024-080.basis: Arunachal Pradesh recorded the lowest density in Census 2011 at 17 persons per sq km.

MPPSC-2021-010.basis: The phosphatase (Scharer) test measures residual alkaline phosphatase in milk to verify pasteurisation; it is not a tea or water test, so "All of the above" is indefensible and the answer is Milk (A). The printed key D is wrong.

MPPSC-2020-008.basis: Coal India Limited has been a Maharatna since 11 April 2011, so it cannot be the answer to a "does not fall under Maharatna" question. The non-Maharatna CPSE in the list is Oil India Limited, a Navratna in 2010 and only elevated to Maharatna on 4 August 2023, long after the January 2020 list the question cites.

MPPSC-2020-032.basis: Kailash Satyarthi was born on 11 January 1954 at Vidisha, Madhya Pradesh, where he studied at the Samrat Ashok Technological Institute. The printed key (Sehore) is wrong; the question's own supplied explanation already said Vidisha.

MPPSC-2020-054.basis: The States Reorganisation Act, 1956 with the Seventh Amendment abolished the Part A/B/C categories and created 14 states and 6 union territories with effect from 1 November 1956. Eighteen states and nine union territories describe a later political map, not the 1956 Act.

MPPSC-2020-076.basis: Bhagwat Dayal Sharma was the first Chief Minister of Haryana (November 1966 to March 1967) and later Governor of Madhya Pradesh (30 April 1980 to 14 May 1984). Ram Naresh Yadav, the printed key, was Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh, so the question's premise does not fit him.

MPPSC-2020-095.basis: PUMA in robotics expands to Programmable Universal Machine for Assembly, the Unimation/Unimation-Scheinman assembly robot. The printed key "Programmed Utility Machine for Assembly" is a reordered distractor; the question's own supplied explanation gave the correct expansion.

MPPSC-2019-027.basis: Section 6(2) of the Protection of Human Rights Act, 1993 makes a Member eligible for re-appointment for another term of five years, so the statement that a Member is not eligible is the only false statement. Statements A, B and D each reproduce the Act, which means the printed key A+B+C marked two true statements as incorrect.

MPPSC-2019-046.basis: Karewas are the lacustrine and glacial clay terraces of the Kashmir valley floor, where saffron is grown, not a landform of the Himachal-Uttarakhand Himalaya. The printed key named the Himachal-Uttarakhand Himalaya, which contradicts both the standard geomorphology and the paper's own explanation.

MPPSC-2019-060.basis: Kathi is a folk dance of the Nimar region of Madhya Pradesh, performed by the Balai community from Dev Prabodhini Ekadashi to Mahashivratri in worship of Parvati. The decorated bamboo kathi is the prop the dancers carry, so 'wooden art' names the object rather than what Kathi is.

MPPSC-2019-074.basis: A keyboard is an input device, so the group keyboard-printer-monitor is not made up only of output devices. Plotter, printer and monitor are all outputs, which is the correct answer.

MPPSC-2019-097.basis: Old NH-3 ran from Agra through Gwalior, Shivpuri, Guna, Dewas and Indore to Mumbai and carried about 712 km in Madhya Pradesh, old NH-12 and old NH-7 also entered the state, but NH-8 ran from Delhi through Jaipur, Udaipur, Ahmedabad and Vadodara to Mumbai without passing through Madhya Pradesh.

MPPSC-2017-100.basis: The IMF lends only to its member countries, not only to developed countries. The stored key B is contradicted by the paper's own explanation and by the identical question at number 85, which the same paper keys C.

MPPSC-2015-045.basis: The Chairman of the Central Pollution Control Board is appointed by the Central Government and is not one of the constitutional office-holders listed; the paper offers None of the above for exactly this reason.

MPPSC-2015-054.basis: Sustainable development rests on the social, economic and environmental pillars together, so the inclusive option is right; the social approach alone is one of three bases.

MPPSC-2015-080.basis: Madhya Pradesh was the first state to implement the 73rd Constitutional Amendment, through the MP Panchayati Raj Act of 1993; Rajasthan's earlier first, at Nagaur in 1959, belongs to panchayati raj before the amendment existed.

MPPSC-2015-097.basis: Alexander Fleming discovered penicillin in 1928; X-rays were discovered by Wilhelm Roentgen in 1895, so the stored key B is contradicted by the facts the question tests.

MPPSC-2014-001.basis: The decision to establish a socialistic pattern of society was taken by the Congress at Avadi in 1955 and became the stated objective of the Second Five year plan; the Fourth Plan (1969-74) pursued growth with stability, so keying D contradicts the record.

MPPSC-2014-065.basis: Under the Protection of Human Rights Act as it stood in 2014 the selection committee for the NHRC consisted of the Prime Minister, the Speaker, the Home Minister, the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha and the Chairman of the Council of States, so the Chairman of the Rajya Sabha was a member and the Leader of the Opposition in the Rajya Sabha was not; the 2019 amendment added that post later.

MPPSC-2014-069.basis: Section 3 of the SC and ST (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989 punishes a public servant who wilfully neglects his duties with imprisonment of not less than six months, extendable to one year; the stored key C is the maximum of that range and the question asks for the minimum.

MPPSC-2013-073.basis: Before the 2010 renumbering of national highways, NH 7 ran from Varanasi to Kanyakumari for about 2,369 km and was the longest highway in India, the stretch now included in NH 44; NH 1 from Delhi to Amritsar is only about 456 km, so the stored key A cannot be reconciled with the record.

MPPSC-2022-045.basis: Ajanta and Bagh are Buddhist rock-cut cave complexes, and Bulsar (Valsad) has none; the printed paper keys Bulsar alone, while the stored two-answer key also named Sanchi, which is a stupa and monastery site rather than a cave site. The official single key is restored and the residual looseness of the question is recorded as an unresolved dispute.
